ns2:section.sectionText: The intent of this seminar is to provide a survey of recent topics in the cognitive neuroscience of memory. Readings will be selected by students to include a wide variety of memory research, including recognition memory, priming, procedural memory, false memory, etc. Each week will be devoted to the readings selected by a student, and to the discussion of (at least) two papers. Students will be responsible for presenting the relevant findings and leading the discussion of the assigned readings, on a rotating basis. The presentation will give us an opportunity to discuss and assess in detail the theory, methods, results, and interpretation associated with that week?s readings.
